title: Derived extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let $\square$ be an
open-immersion square and let
$\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For every
$K\in D^+(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the map of
[lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] is an isomorphism

$$
g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!g_U^{-1}K
$$

in $D^+(X'_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and the isomorphism is natural in $K$,
is the identity for $g=\operatorname{id}$, and is compatible with
pasting of open-immersion squares.

proof.text: Use the existing constant-coefficient sheaf functors upperStar and openImmersionLowerShriek with A = ModuleCat Λ. Their source instances supply additivity and exactness. The existing exact-functor constructions apply termwise to complexes, localize, and preserve the bounded-below subcategories. Keep the two public definitions of the canonical exchange and extension-by-zero composition comparisons unchanged.

source.place: Tag 015F; existing exact sheaf-functor instances in UpperLowerStar.Defs and LowerShriek.OpenImmersion.Defs

proof.text: The canonical underived map β is characterized by its unit equation. Apply mateEquiv_eq_of_unit to unit_map_openImmersionLowerShriekBaseChangeMap_app: its mate under j_! ⊣ j^* and j'_! ⊣ j'^* is exactly squareUpperStarIso for the flipped commuting square. Its inverse is the base-change map used in the public derived definition. Invertibility and naturality of the derived map then follow from the natural isomorphism itself.

For the identity square, prove the underived unit law by injectivity of mateEquiv. The mate of the normalized identity square is computed by mateEquiv_unitors. Expanding squareUpperStarIso and applying upperStarComp_id_left and upperStarComp_id_right gives that same mate. Cancel the identity comparison to obtain β_id followed by upperStarId_X equals j_! applied to upperStarId_U.

source.place: Tag 03S6, identity adjunction and inverse-image unit laws

proof.text: For successive base changes, compare the mates of β for the composite square and the composite of the two β maps with the upperStarComp comparisons. mateEquiv_whiskerTop_whiskerBottom and mateEquiv_vcomp reduce equality to squareUpperStarIso_paste_vert_hom. For composable open immersions, first show that the conjugate of the actual openImmersionLowerShriekComp is upperStarComp.symm, using Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app. Then conjugateEquiv/mateEquiv composition and mateEquiv_hcomp reduce the required equality of mates to squareUpperStarIso_paste_horiz_hom. Injectivity gives both precise underived pasting equations.

source.place: Tag 03S6; canonical extension-by-zero composition through uniqueness of left adjoints

proof.text: Prove the derived identity law directly by localization. The factorization formulas for mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso, mapDerivedCategoryPlusIdIso and mapDerivedCategoryPlusSquareIso reduce equality after precomposition with the homotopy-category localization functor Qh to the underived identity law. Naturality of the factorization maps cancels their comparisons; faithfulness of the bounded-below inclusion and the homotopy quotient reduce the remaining equality to its component in each complex degree. Localization.natTrans_ext then gives the equality for every derived object.

source.place: Tag 015F; categories.tex Tag 04VG, detection of natural transformations under localization

proof.text: Use the existing generic mapDerivedCategoryPlusSquareIso_comp twice, with the exact functors and precise underived pasting equations proved above. For successive base changes apply it to the inverse canonical mates and the upperStarComp comparisons; for composable opens apply it to the forward mates and openImmersionLowerShriekComp. Private proved identities show that localization preserves inversion of the natural isomorphisms and identify the generic square/composition comparisons with the two unchanged public definitions. Cancel the invertible comparisons and exchange maps to obtain exactly the two displayed derived pasting clauses.

source.place: Tag 015F; categories.tex Tag 04VG, functorial localization of compositions
